dataList.content:
Warning, warning. Land ahoy.
警告，警告。接近陆地。
dataList.place:
Cabins of Mephistopheles
梅菲斯托费勒斯 船舱

dataList.content:
Charon, who had been quietly holding the helm for a while, suddenly spoke up. As if on cue, everyone in the cabin simultaneously jumped up from their seats. The crew's joy at the end of this long journey was palpable.
一直安静地握着舵的卡戎突然冒出的一句话，让船舱里的每个人都高兴得跳了起来，发出的欢呼声交织在了一起。

Finally! Is it over?!
终于！要结束了吗？！

My eyes well with tears of relief...
我快要落泪了……

Haah... If they ever let us go on a vacation, remind me to preclude any seafaring options. I think I've had enough of the Great Lake for one lifetime...
哈啊……如果接下来要去哪里玩的话绝对不能去有船的地方。我这辈子都受够了……

Some Sinners began to visibly relax with the realization that the long Lake voyage had finally come to an end. Others rushed to the windows as if they were expecting anything to have changed while we were away from the shores.
一些人因为大湖上的生活终于要结束了而松了一口气，而另一些人则紧紧贴着窗户向外看，想要确认这段时间里陆地是否发生了什么变化。

You guys are being so overdramatic. Back in my sailor days, setting sail in the Great Lake meant that you'd have to spend—
太夸张了吧……我那时候，上了船可就是3年起步……

—at least three years at the treacherous sea, out of any landsmen's sight. Right. I think I've heard that exact sentence a few dozen times by now. So...
这话，感觉在湖上漂流的时候我就已经听过几十遍了，就别说了吧……

... Agreed. You have made your point, Ishmael. I found it difficult to tolerate when you began sharing that story for the fourth time.
别太过分，以实玛利。事不过三。

Khm... Y-you guys were the ones who complained that no one had any fun stories to tell.
嗯……哈，我只是因为你说你无话可说才提起这事的……

Just as we were exchanging a few meaningless jabs at each other...
就在以为这些无聊的谈话会继续下去的时候……

BOOM!
哐嘡！

... Mephistopheles suddenly jerked violently as though something had exploded.
梅菲斯托费勒斯突然一震，然后开始猛烈晃动。

Of course, we were all promptly thrown about the busboat like ragdolls.
当然……我们所有人都在其中被震得飞了起来或是滚来滚去。

Augh...
啊啊……

<I-is everyone okay?!>
<大、大家都没事吧？>

Oww... Can this bloody bus come to a smooth stop for once...?
啊啊啊……这该死的巴士，怎么就不能顺顺当当地停下来一次呢……
dataList.place:
Aboard Mephistopheles
梅菲斯托费勒斯 内部

dataList.content:
Wait, bus?
诶，巴士？

Heathcliff was right. I took a quick look around...
希斯克利夫说得没错，仔细一看周围……

... and realized that the cabins had transformed back to the shape of the bus we'd grown so used to.
船舱变回了我们熟悉的巴士的形态。

Charon hit the transform button. Click clack.
卡戎，刚按下变形按钮。咔嗒咔嗒。

Charon... can you give us a warning for once? At least a turn signal or something? Please!
先打开指示灯再按行吗……喂！

Yeah, Charon. Please...
卡戎，拜托了……

Busboat don't have turn signals. Too bad, Bug Guy.
巴士船没有指示灯。没有办法，虫男。

Haaaaah...
哈啊啊……

<I thought there was going to be some complicated procedure to transform it back to a bus... I guess it just happens with the click of a button, huh.>
<还以为会有什么复杂的程序，竟然这样就变回来了……>

I thought we'd have to stop by a workshop or a boatworks office again...
我还以为我们必须要再去一趟工坊、修船厂之类的地方呢……

One of many functions of Mephistopheles is that it can remember every form or property it once possessed.
梅菲斯托费勒斯有着能记忆曾经被刻印的性质的机能。

Therefore, it follows that once it takes a certain form, it can revert to it or any of its previous forms at any time.
一旦拥有了某种形态，就可以直接进入别的形态，也可以再变回去。

I-I see...
是、是这样啊……

Anyways~ We're finally back on land! Aren't you glad, Heathcliff? You've been so looking forward to this!
总之~很高兴你平安抵达了你期待已久的陆地，希斯克利夫先生！

Huh? OH! Ohh...
嗯？啊！啊……

Heathcliff's face lit up for a brief second before a vortex of complicated feelings overcame him.
希斯克利夫的表情稍微明朗了一些，然后他马上又露出一副复杂的表情。

Then... Oi, vroom-vroom lass. Are we at... T Corp.?
也就是说……喂，嘀嘀叭叭。这里是……T公司吗？

Heathcliff was talking to Charon, but she did not reply. Maybe it was because he didn't call her by her name—or maybe it was that she didn't really know where we were either. She always drives wherever her whims take her, after all.
希斯克利夫向卡戎问道，但不知道是因为没有叫自己的名字，还是因为只是像往常一样专心开车，她什么都没有回答。

This monochromatic, grey hue is reminiscent of that place, indeed. Yet... there is a disparity.
灰色的样子和夺走颜色的那个地方很像……但又有点不一样。

Hm... Yeah? I suppose it was of a different monochromatic hue than whatever this is.
嗯……是吗。好像不是这种颜色。

T Corp... District 20... I've never been there myself, but I've tangentially experienced it via Yi Sang's Fathoms of Ego.
T公司……20区……虽然没有亲自去过，但确实是在李箱的自我心道中经历过的地方。

Yeah... that place was supposed to take our colors away, wasn't it?
似乎是颜色被夺走的地方……

Have some patience, Heathcliff. We are still in the Backstreets.
放松点，希斯克利夫。这里还只是后巷而已。

We are getting quite close to the place you know so well... aren't we?
只不过是你长期置身于其中的地方的入口。

<Vergilius, you had no reason to provoke him like that...>
<没必要故意刺激他吧……>

Is there a reason we're going through the Backstreets instead of heading straight to the Nest?
不直接进入巢，反而从后巷走是有什么理由吗？

<Huh, you're right. Why are we going through the Backstreets anyway?>
<啊，是啊。那点我也很好奇。>

I am curious as well. The Backstreets roads are rife with danger and winding, roundabout paths. This carries an unnecessary risk, does it not?
我也很好奇。穿过后巷的道路有很多绕行路线，我认为会增加时间和危险因素。

I would also like to highlight that the immigration process is significantly more lenient when one is migrating from a Nest to a Nest than it is when migrating from the Backstreets to a Nest territory.
从巢直接进入巢的许可，比经由后巷进入的审查条件更为宽松。

Ishmael's question to Vergilius had opened a whole new floodgate of questions from other Sinners.
以实玛利的话让其他罪人们也七嘴八舌起来。

Hm... Looks like you have all grown rather chatty since we first met.
嗯……最近各位的问题变多了啊。

You must know that it won't change how I choose to answer your questions. Ask me all you want, but I will not spare the time to give you a comprehensible explanation for your convenience.
我不会亲切地进行说明的方针，应该不会改变。

What's wrong with asking for some explanations if we're being led through a questionable path?
如果对方向产生疑问的话，难道不应该询问吗？

It is your job as our guide to tell us where to go, isn't it?
向导的工作不就是指明方向么。

Don't tell me that we haven't been authorized to enter T Corp.'s Nest yet? And here I thought Limbus Company was a proper business.
难道说，没有得到T公司的出入许可吗？边狱公司不是正经公司吗？

Sure, it's relatively new. But I thought we had a rather 'substantial backing'?
再怎么是新生公司，不也是个后盾很坚实的公司吗？

We can receive proper authorization to enter most Nests should we request it.
当然可以得到大部分巢的出入许可。

Then why—
那为什么……

It's the company's will.
是公司的意思。

Vergilius silenced the entire hubbub on the bus with a short but low growl.
维吉里乌斯低沉、粗哑的声音让骚动停了下来。

My job as your guide is to plan a path toward the destination as requested by the company.
向导的工作是调整公司委托的目的地的行进方法。

Selecting this path was also a part of accommodating that request. So... please, know your place and shut your mouth.
选择这个路径也只是按照那个意思的结果……哈。希望你们能适当地闭嘴。

Perhaps the commotion was getting to him. I could tell that Vergilius was rubbing his ear out of frustration.
维吉里乌斯像嫌吵一样，一脸烦躁地摆弄着耳朵说。

Well, if that's the case...
好吧……既然是那样。

While doubt was still apparent on Ishmael's face, she nodded affirmatively. She was acknowledging that there was little we could do about the orders from the company itself.
即使不能接受，但既然是公司的命令也无可奈何。正当以实玛利这么想着，准备点头的时候。

... Huh. That alarm again... Is someone listening in on us or something? That was one conveniently timed alarm, don'tcha think?
……哈，又是警报……难道是在偷听我们说话？时机这么巧真的好么？

That is unlikely.
应该没有那种可能。

Dante.
但丁。

Like always, Faust looked into the bus' terminal before giving me a look that I've come to recognize.
浮士德像往常一样看了看巴士的终端，然后望向我。

<Yep... another volatility to take care of, huh?>
<唔……我们还得再去一次对吗？>

Yes, it is.
是的，没错。

Another one? Didn't we JUST wrap up a Backdoor volatility?
又来？之前后门变化的时候我们不是才去过么？

Oh... I think I know what this is.
啊……我好像懂了。

First were the Mirror Dungeons and the Luxcavation Dungeons.
之前是镜像迷宫……采光迷宫发生了变化。

So it's gotta be...
那么剩下的就是……

Faust considers Herr Gregor's growing aptitude for deductions to be a positive development.
对于格里高尔先生的推理能力与日俱增，浮士德表示肯定。

Haah... it's the Refraction Railway, isn't it.
哈啊……折射轨道吗。

The bus soon fills with the Sinners' exasperated sighs.
罪人们纷纷叹气。

Sod it... it's that bloody subway tracks again.
妈的……又是那该死的地铁。

Aww... Railways really wear me out every time we enter.
啊~每次去都会筋疲力尽呢……

Well, since the last one was called 'Line 2'... is this going to be 'Line 3'?
之前是2号线……这么说的话，接下来应该是3号线了？

That is likely, yes. Though we cannot say for certain before observing it for ourselves.
那样的可能性很高。但是在直接前往观察之前都无法确定。

Dante.
但丁。

<I know, I know...>
<我知道了……>

Going through the Refraction Railways takes a lot out of me, too.
折射轨道是连我也会产生相当疲劳感的空间。

So far, each Refraction Railway has had new and different patterns, and enemies we faced in there were all much more powerful than any other enemies we'd faced before.
每当出现的时候，轨道的特征也会发生变化，会有比至今为止遇到的敌人更强大的家伙。

... it's also true that I see a noticeable improvement in most Sinners' combat prowess once we've had a run through the Railway.
经历过一次轨道后，罪人们的战斗方式和熟练度明显增加也是事实。

Not to mention the copious amount of rewards.
更不用提所获得的大量报酬。

I don't remember exactly when it was, but Faust once took the time to explain the Railways' Abnormalities to me.
虽然记不清楚是什么时候，但浮士德曾经对轨道的异想体进行过说明。

That the Abnormalities we battle in the Railways are probably not the same ones that exist in the world that we live in.
在轨道上遇见的东西，并不是我们现在所在的世界里原本的存在。

So... it's not like we'll be able to capture them and bring them back, but they're perfect for practice just in case we run into their real versions.
所以……即使镇压也不存在可以回收的好处，但是正好适合预习面对实物时的应对方法。

Well, whichever is the case... going through the Railway will be a net positive for us.
一一列举利弊，证明还是前往轨道会更有利。

So...
所以……

<Let's get going, then.>
<出发吧。>

I took a quick glance at the Sinners...
我环顾了一眼罪人们……

... then opened the door to the Backdoor.
打开了通向后门的大门。
